fields.meta_title: Employee Benefits Survey Builder for HR Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee benefits survey from a prompt: rank what staff value, rate each plan, and find benefits few know about. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Benefits Survey Before Your Next Renewal
fields.hero_description: Build an employee benefits survey that ranks what staff value, rates each plan, and saves answers to a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: What Emergent builds behind an employee benefits survey, from the first question to the results HR brings to renewal.
fields.feature_1:
Drafted from the benefits you offer

List the plans and perks you pay for today and the ones under review. Emergent drafts use, rating, and priority questions for each, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen on a phone

Staff without a desk answer on their phones from a link you post in the break room. The survey shows one question per screen, and a 12-question survey reads like a short chat.
fields.feature_3:
Each answer filed with role, site, and shift

Every response is saved in a database you own, next to the role, site, and shift the employee picked. Compare hourly with salaried staff on any single benefit you offer.
fields.feature_4:
An alert when a benefit scores low

Set the line yourself, such as 20 or more people saying they never use a plan. The app emails your HR lead or posts in a Slack channel once the answers cross that line.
fields.feature_5:
No cap on how many people answer

Survey a 40-person office or a 4,000-person workforce on the same build. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and every employee who opens the link can finish the survey.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, exported on paid plans

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans, then run next year's survey from the same build, with this year's answers still sitting in your tables.

fields.tab_content_1:
The 401(k) match takes 31 of 100 points

Marrow Lane Credit Union gives each employee 100 points to split across 6 benefits it could fund next year. Before the renewal meeting, 212 people answered. The 401(k) match averaged 31 points and extra PTO 24, while the childcare stipend averaged 9. Each split is saved with the employee's branch.
fields.tab_content_2:
HR gets an email when dental scores 2.6

Pellham Machine Works asked 148 employees to rate each current benefit from 1 to 5. HR set one line: any benefit averaging under 3.0 goes to the renewal review. Dental came in at 2.6 out of 5, while vision scored 4.1. The app emailed HR director Joel Brandt the dental result and its 148 ratings before the broker meeting.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two benefits that fewer than half knew about

Oakhaven Software asked 150 employees one yes-or-no question per benefit: did you know this was offered? Any benefit that fewer than half knew about goes to the #benefits channel in Slack. Only 57 of 150 knew the employee assistance program (EAP), and 69 of 150 knew pet insurance.
fields.tab_content_4:
Shifts split on $40 a month or 2 days off

Sorrel Distribution posts the survey link at the time clock for its 210 hourly staff, and it opens on a phone. Of those 210, 164 answered one trade-off: $40 a month toward the health premium, or 2 more paid days off. Night shift picked the premium help 48 to 24. Day shift picked the days off 55 to 37.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Employee Benefits Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an employee benefits survey whose answers show which benefits to keep and which to change at renewal.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose the groups you will compare
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add one question that forces a choice
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every benefit you pay for today, from the medical plan to the commuter subsidy. Then add the 2 or 3 options you could fund next year. Put the full list in your prompt, and Emergent drafts a section for each benefit.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide which groups matter before you write a question: site, full-time or part-time, tenure band, or whether someone covers dependents. Ask for the group instead of a name, and keep each group large enough that no single person stands out.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Open each benefit by asking whether the person knew about it and used it in the past year. Show the rating only to people who used it. A 1 from someone who never filed a dental claim then stays out of the dental average.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A rating grid lets people mark every benefit as important. Add one question with a fixed budget, such as 100 points to split or a choice between two options, and the answers will show what employees would give up to get something else.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to 5 employees, one from each site or shift you plan to compare. Ask where they hesitated and which question they read twice. Reword those questions with a follow-up prompt before the survey goes to everyone.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Open it for 2 weeks, remind once
fields.howto_step_6_des: Keep the survey open for 2 weeks so every shift sees it. On day 5, have the app post a reminder with the closing date in a company Slack channel, or email it to everyone on the list.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sort the benefits by average rating and by points, then read the comments next to the lowest score. Bring that view and the group splits to the meeting with your broker, and decide which plan to change first.

faq_plan.q: What is an employee benefits survey?
faq_plan.a: An employee benefits survey is a questionnaire that asks employees which benefits they use, how well each one works for them, and which matter most. HR runs it ahead of a plan renewal or open enrollment to decide what to keep and what to change.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an employee benefits survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the survey in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: the benefits you offer, the groups you want to compare, and the rating scale. Emergent builds the questions, the logic, and a results dashboard, and saves every response in a database you own. Change any question with a follow-up prompt.

faq_plan.q: What questions should be included in an employee benefits survey?
faq_plan.ref: What questions should be included in an employee benefits survey?

prov.original: What questions should be included in an employee benefits survey?

faq_plan.a: Good employee benefits survey questions cover four things for each benefit: whether people know it exists, whether they have claimed or used it lately, how satisfied they are with it, and how it ranks against the others. Add one open question about what is missing, plus group questions such as site and tenure band.

faq_plan.q: What does a sample employee benefits survey look like?
faq_plan.a: A sample employee benefits survey runs in five parts: group questions, an awareness check per benefit, 1-to-5 ratings for the benefits each person used, a 100-point split across options, and one open question. Keep questions about managers and workload for an employee satisfaction survey. On Emergent, the sample is a starting prompt you can reshape by asking for changes.

faq_plan.q: When is the best time to run an employee benefits satisfaction survey?
faq_plan.a: Run it 8 to 12 weeks before the plan renewal date. That leaves time to tally the answers and take them to your broker before the quotes are final. Repeat it once a year at the same point in the cycle, and each year's scores line up with the last.

faq_plan.q: How is an employee benefits survey different from a benefits benchmarking report?
faq_plan.a: An employee benefits survey asks your own employees what they use and value; a benchmarking report shows what other employers offer. The SHRM Employee Benefits Survey is an annual survey of HR professionals that reports over 230 unique employee benefits. KFF's Employer Health Benefits Survey is an annual survey of employers with ten or more workers.

faq_plan.q: Should employee benefits survey questions run as their own survey?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the benefits package is up for renewal. Give it its own send date, apart from other surveys. If you already run an employee engagement survey, add 3 or 4 benefits questions to it in the years between full rounds to follow the trend.

faq_plan.q: How many employee benefit survey questions should you ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask 12 to 20 questions, and cut any question whose answer would not change a renewal decision. For 8 benefits, that is one awareness item and one rating each, plus a priority question and 3 group questions. With no response cap on Emergent, the length of the survey is the only limit you manage.

faq_plan.q: Should an employee benefits survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for the ratings and comments. Leave out name and email fields, ask for shift and department instead, and show a group's results only once 5 or more people in it have answered. With Emergent, those answers sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How should you share employee benefits survey results with staff?
faq_plan.a: Post a one-page summary within 2 weeks of the survey closing: the top employee priority, the lowest-rated benefit, and what HR will do about each. Name each change, such as a new dental carrier, and the date it starts. After open enrollment, a 3-question pulse survey shows whether people understood the change.

This page is the benefits preference survey itself: four surveys built from a prompt, each ending in a decision before renewal (a 100-point priority split, plan ratings that flag a weak plan, an awareness check that finds unknown benefits, a phone survey that shows shifts want different things), with the FAQ covering the questions to ask, timing, anonymity and how an internal survey differs from a benchmark report. Pay belongs to the compensation survey sibling and job satisfaction to the employee satisfaction sibling.

intent.evidence: Builder-fit with benefits-preference angle: question set (FAQ 3), sample structure (FAQ 4), 7-step how-to, four worked surveys; FAQ 6 separates own survey from SHRM/KFF benchmark reports that hold the top 10.

truth.evidence: SHRM annual HR-professional survey and 230+ benefits, KFF ten-or-more-workers survey quoted in domain_sources; definition sourced (Qualtrics). No benefits, legal or state-specific advice. Numbers: 31+24+18+11+9+7=100; 2.6<3.0; 57/150 and 69/150 under half; 48+24+37+55=164 of 210.

distinct.evidence: Engagement, satisfaction and pulse surveys linked as separate tools, not headlined.

faq.evidence: PAA item 3 verbatim; written questions page-specific with at most one secondary each; no brand in questions; no third-party pricing; no link-only endings.
